newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil group expects suit over cleaner air moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil group expects suit over cleaner air moves.

text.p: The head of the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday that he expects a legal battle if the government decides to tighten controversial air quality standards in July.

"I predict someone will sue," said Charles DiBona, president of API. "This (proposal) has a lot of implications for the economy of this country but there is no scientific evidence that there would be any health benefits from this."
DiBona, echoing earlier API statements, told reporters his group was strongly opposed to the proposal as it now stands. The EPA could pass the proposal by early this summer.
DiBona did not say if the API would itself file a lawsuit, but said the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposal bordered on "arbitrary and capricious behavoir."
He noted the EPA, which proposed the standards last November, has the power to set rules, but Congress has the power to possibly reject them.

The standards would impose tougher limits on smog and fine dust and soot particulates from power plants, refineries and other sources. The Agency has said it is proposing more stringent federal air quality standards because current requirements do not adequately protect the public's health.
But DiBona said the standards would cost billions of dollars to implement, and affect millions of motorists and business owners in increased gasoline costs and factory upgrades.
The API is one of 800 members of a coalition that includes farmers, electric companies and mining associations that are against the new standards.
The Air Quality Standard Coalition also has the backing of five Democratic senators and several Republican and Democratic governors.

They claim the studies the EPA used to measure the health benefits of the new standards were inaccurate and incomplete, a point challenged by supporters, including the American Lung Association. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
